item.title: String functions and cyclotomic Hecke algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.22669v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we study the Kleshchev multipartitions that label simple modules of certain cyclotomic Hecke algebras with parameters $1$ and $-1$. The $2$-residue statistic divides these multipartitions into blocks. We deduce a bivariate generating function for the blocks using representation theory. We also relate the generating functions of multipartitions in a fixed block to string functions associated by Kac and Peterson to irreducible highest weight modules of a type $A_1^{(1)}$ affine Lie algebra. By considering matrices formed by these generating functions, we reprove some results of Kac--Peterson on string functions using the Macdonald identities of Rosengren--Schlosser. As an application, we obtain new infinite product formulas for these generating functions.
item.dc:creator: Dennis Stanton, Ting Xue, Ae Ja Yee

item.title: Typical representations of admissible type I algebraic supergroups
item.description: arXiv:2610.23055v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study typical representations of an admissible type I algebraic supergroup $G$. We prove that, for a dominant weight $\lambda$, the induced supermodule $H^0_G(\lambda)$ is simple if and only if $\lambda$ is typical and the induced module $H^0_{G_{\mathrm{ev}}}(\lambda)$ for the even subgroup $G_{\mathrm{ev}}$ is simple. We establish equivalences between typical blocks for $G$ and blocks for $G_{\mathrm{ev}}$, and give a projectivity criterion for Kac modules over every Frobenius kernel. For connected $SpO(2\ell|2)$ over an algebraically closed field of odd characteristic, we classify all simple projective supermodules over Frobenius kernels.
item.dc:creator: Taiki Shibata

item.title: Whittaker Functionals for Exceptional Representations
item.description: arXiv:2610.23169v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the study of automorphic forms on covering groups, Kazhdan-Patterson gives a formula that determines when the Whittaker functionals of induced representations can be descended to exceptional representations. In this paper, first, following the original approach given by Kazhdan-Patterson and applying the block-compatible 2-cocycle of Banks-Levy-Sepanski, we fill in several details omitted in the original proof. Secondly, we compare the formula of Kazhdan-Patterson with that of McNamara and Gao, which is formulated in a more general setting.
item.dc:creator: Sihan Li

item.title: Trilinear Forms for ${\rm GL}_2(\mathbb{F}_q)$ via conjugacy classes
item.description: arXiv:2610.23450v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: It is well known that for a finite group \(G\), the number of elements in ${\rm Irr}(G)$ the set of irreducible representations up to isomorphism is the same as the number of elements in ${\rm Conj}(G)$ the set of conjugacy classes in $G$ although there is no natural bijection between these two sets. For $G={\rm GL}_2(\mathbb{F}_q)$, where $\mathbb{F}_q$ is the finite field with $q$ elements, we give a bijection between ${\rm Irr}(G)$ and ${\rm Conj}(G)$, which behaves well with the tensor product of irreducible representations on one side and the product of conjugacy classes on the other. In particular, we relate the dimension of the trilinear forms with the multiplicity of the identity element in the triple product of the corresponding conjugacy classes.
item.dc:creator: Ankita Parashar, Shiv Prakash Patel

item.title: Plancherel Decompositions and Distinctions for $\mathrm{Sp}_{2n}\backslash \mathrm{Gl}_{2n+1}$ and $P(\mathrm{Sp}_{2n})\backslash \mathrm{Gl}_{2n}$
item.description: arXiv:2610.23737v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $F$ be a non-Archimedean local field of characteristic zero. We determine the Plancherel decompositions of $\mathrm{Sp}_{2n}(F)\backslash\mathrm{GL}_{2n+1}(F)$ and $P(\mathrm{Sp}_{2n})(F)\backslash\mathrm{GL}_{2n}(F)$, where $P(\mathrm{Sp}_{2n})$ denotes the mirabolic subgroup of $\mathrm{Sp}_{2n}$, and study smooth distinction for both spaces. We carry out the local unfolding procedure of arXiv:1203.0039, Section 9.5, constructing unitary isomorphisms with degenerate Whittaker models by successive Fourier transforms. The isomorphism for the even model is already stated there in Example 9.5.17. The resulting Plancherel formulas are direct integrals of normalized parabolic inductions from the tempered duals of $\mathrm{GL}_n(F)\times\mathrm{GL}_{n+1}(F)$ and $\mathrm{GL}_n(F)\times\mathrm{GL}_n(F)$, respectively, with product Whittaker-Plancherel measures. In the odd case, the parameter map agrees with the prediction of arXiv:2409.04677. Using closed parabolic orbits and local Rankin-Selberg integrals, we prove that all representations induced from these tempered data are distinguished for the corresponding model. We also prove that essentially square-integrable representations are not distinguished for the odd model, and that supercuspidal representations are not distinguished for the even model. For the even model with $n=1,2$, we construct distinguished square-integrable representations outside the Plancherel support. Thus, the smooth tempered distinguished spectrum can be strictly larger than the corresponding $L^2$-spectrum. For $\mathrm{GL}_5(F)$, however, we prove that an irreducible tempered representation is $\mathrm{Sp}_4(F)$-distinguished if and only if it is induced from tempered representations of $\mathrm{GL}_2(F)$ and $\mathrm{GL}_3(F)$.
item.dc:creator: Sagnik Mukherjee

item.title: The Schubert bialgebra
item.description: arXiv:2610.22582v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce a Schubert bialgebra $\mathcal{A}=\bigoplus_{n\geq 0}\mathbb{Z}[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$, in which polynomials in different numbers of variables multiply to zero and the coproduct splits the variables into two consecutive blocks, and study its graded dual $\mathcal{D}$, whose product is concatenation of weak compositions. The Schubert polynomials $\mathfrak{S}_u^n$ form a basis of $\mathcal{A}$; we give an explicit formula for the dual Schubert basis $\Xi_u^n$ of $\mathcal{D}$ via a transition formula to an elementary symmetric basis, and show that the Schubert structure constants $c_{u,v}^w$ are the coefficients of the coproduct of $\mathcal{D}$ in the dual Schubert basis. The product of $\mathcal{D}$ is then lifted to an associative product $\sqcup$ on the free abelian group $\mathcal{BRC}$ of bounded RC graphs, built from a transition map $\mathcal{Z}$ on RC graphs that realizes the Lascoux-Sch\"utzenberger transition formula and generalizes Little's bumping algorithm. Quotienting $\mathcal{BRC}$ by ideals coming from Demazure crystal equivalence, Nadeau-Tewari forest equivalence, and quasi-Yamanouchi equivalence yields manifestly positive Littlewood-Richardson rules for the dual Schubert, dual key, dual forest, and dual slide bases of $\mathcal{D}$. Read on $\mathcal{A}$, these are branching rules: enumerative formulas for splitting a Schubert, key, forest, or slide polynomial across two blocks of variables, and in the Schubert case they compute the Levi branching coefficients of Ressayre-Richmond for $\mathrm{GL}_p\times\mathrm{GL}_q\hookrightarrow\mathrm{GL}_{p+q}$.
item.dc:creator: Matthew J. Samuel

item.title: Classification of real Lie algebras of dimension one, two and three
item.description: arXiv:2610.23000v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present an exhaustive, self-contained, and coordinate-free structural classification of real Lie algebras of dimensions one, two, and three up to isomorphism. In dimensions one and two, the classification is governed entirely by the derived ideal and elementary derivation theory. In dimension three, we develop the classical exterior duality isomorphism $\Lambda^2\mathfrak{g} \cong \mathfrak{g}^* \otimes \Lambda^3\mathfrak{g}$ pioneered by Bryant and Milnor, which reduces the quadratic Jacobi identity on the $3 \times 3$ structure matrix $C = S + \hat{a}$ to the linear orthogonality relation $S \cdot a = 0$, where $a = \frac{1}{2}\chi$ is the trace covector. We systematically bifurcate the three-dimensional category into unimodular ($a = 0$) and non-unimodular ($a \neq 0$) sectors, completely recovering the nine classical Bianchi isomorphism classes (Bianchi types I through IX) alongside their continuous moduli invariants. Furthermore, we establish the Levi--Malcev decomposition for low dimensions, compute the exact minimal representation dimension $\mu(\mathfrak{g})$ via Ado's Theorem by constructing explicit matrix realizations in $\mathfrak{gl}(\mu, \mathbb{R})$, and formulate a deterministic, coordinate-free decision algorithm for algebra identification.
item.dc:creator: Mehdi Nadjafikhah

item.title: Phases in the cyclic quantum dilogarithm: correction to "Cyclic quantum Teichm\"uller theory"
item.description: arXiv:2610.23572v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We first correct $\boldsymbol{\mu}_N$-phase issues in the basic definition around the cyclic quantum dilogarithm operators in [Ish26]. In particular, the notion of global coefficients must be extended by incorporating additional lifting data forming a $\boldsymbol{\mu}_N$-cover, and the pentagon relation generally acquires an extra $\boldsymbol{\mu}_N$-factor. Nevertheless, we prove that every point in a regular locus of the partially compactified cluster Poisson variety lifts to a \emph{strict} extended global coefficient, for which this extra $\boldsymbol{\mu}_N$-factor is trivial. Consequently, the original statements of [Ish26] hold for such lifts and are therefore restored.
item.dc:creator: Tsukasa Ishibashi

item.title: Locally Gorenstein algebras, a generalization of Gorenstein algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.23592v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For an Artin algebra $\Lambda$, we define the class of locally Gorenstein modules, which is a generalization of semi-Gorenstein projective modules and, therefore, a generalization of projective Gorenstein modules. For a locally Gorenstein module $X\in{\rm mod}\ \Lambda$ we construct $\underline{{\chi}}_X$ a subcategory of $\underline{{\rm mod}}$ $\Lambda$ and we prove that the syzygy functor is faithful and full on $\underline{{\chi}}_X$. Using that, we prove that the Igusa-Todorov functions $\phi$ and $\psi$ vanish on the family of locally Gorenstein modules. Finally, using locally Gorenstein modules, we define the locally Gorenstein algebras, a generalization of Gorenstein algebras, and we prove that their finitistic, and the $\phi$ and $\psi$ dimensions are finite.
item.dc:creator: Leonardo Alarcon, Mar\'ia Andrea Gatica, Marcelo Lanzilotta

item.title: Totally elliptic surface group representations
item.description: arXiv:2411.19748v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A surface group representation into a Lie group is called totally elliptic if every simple closed curve on the surface is mapped to an elliptic element of the target group. In this note, we characterize all totally elliptic surface group representations into $\mathrm{PSL}_2\mathbb{R}$ and $\mathrm{PSL}_2\mathbb{C}$ by showing that they are either representations into a compact subgroup or Deroin--Tholozan representations.
item.dc:creator: Arnaud Maret

item.title: Stable Brauer--Thrall II$'$ conjecture for finite-dimensional Jacobian algebras
item.description: arXiv:2512.06623v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that finite-dimensional Jacobian algebras associated with non-degenerate quivers with potentials satisfy the stable Brauer--Thrall II$'$ conjecture. In particular, this implies that the brick Brauer--Thrall II$'$ conjecture (also known as the $\tau$-Brauer--Thrall II$'$ conjecture) holds for finite-dimensional Jacobian algebras.
item.dc:creator: Mohamad Haerizadeh, Toshiya Yurikusa

item.title: Wide Regular Subalgebras of Symmetrizable Kac-Moody Algebras and an Extension of Schur's Lemma
item.description: arXiv:2606.01371v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The behavior of representations under restriction is a central theme in Lie theory. We study wide regular subalgebras of symmetrizable Kac--Moody algebras, extending work of Douglas and Repka on semisimple Lie algebras. A subalgebra is \emph{wide} if every irreducible integrable highest weight module remains indecomposable upon restriction. Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a symmetrizable Kac--Moody algebra with Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak{h}$, root system $\Phi$, simple roots $\Pi$, and root space decomposition $\mathfrak{g}=\mathfrak{h}\oplus\bigoplus_{\alpha\in\Phi}\mathfrak{g}_\alpha$. Denote by $\Phi_{\operatorname{re}}$ the set of real roots. To a regular subalgebra $\mathfrak{s}$ normalized by $\mathfrak{h}$, we associate a subset $T\subseteq \Phi$ by declaring $\alpha\in T$ if $\mathfrak{s}\cap \mathfrak{g}_\alpha\ne \{0\}$. One of our main results is an extension of Schur's lemma: if $\mathfrak{h}\subseteq \mathfrak{s}$ and the real closure of $(T\cup(-T))\cap \Phi_{\operatorname{re}}$ contains $\Pi$, then $(\operatorname{End} V)^{\mathfrak{s}}=\mathbb{C}\operatorname{Id}_V$ for every irreducible integrable highest weight module $V$. As a consequence, this real-root closure condition yields a sufficient condition for wideness. In the affine case, we establish a necessary condition for wideness: if $\mathfrak{s}$ is wide, then the closure of $T\cup(-T)$ in $\Phi$ is all of $\Phi$, and this implication holds without assuming that $\mathfrak{h}\subseteq \mathfrak{s}$. A key ingredient is a structural result showing that closed subsets of affine root systems are closed under arbitrary finite root sums that remain roots.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Douglas, Abid Ali

item.title: Quasi-equivalence of relabeled positroid cluster structures
item.description: arXiv:2609.30637v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove the Fraser--Sherman-Bennett conjecture on the quasi-equivalence of positroid cluster structures arising from admissibly relabeled plabic graphs. We construct a tilting module from the boundary necklace and obtain a Frobenius categorification of the relabeled cluster structure. By identifying localized characters of rank-one modules with Pl\"ucker coordinates, we match the stable images of the mutable face modules with the summands of a reachable cluster-tilting object in the stable category. The induced derived equivalence yields a unimodular transformation of relative index lattices intertwining the full extended exchange matrices. These comparisons show that the identity map on the coordinate ring is a quasi-cluster isomorphism between the two cluster structures.
item.dc:creator: Yilin Wu

item.title: Multiplicity One and van Dijk's Conjecture for Connected Complex Symmetric Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.14540v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove regularity for symmetric pairs of connected complex reductive groups by combining invariant theory with the analysis of Schwartz distributions. For the classical residual families, a Gaussian lifting argument reduces the required equivariant vanishing to invariant theory in quadratic moment quotients: contraction and supertrace identities settle DIII and balanced CII, while Gram-matrix invariants and volume tensors handle BDI/Spin. In the exceptional EVII case, transverse slices and explicit radial differential operators establish the vanishing of the full sign-equivariant Schwartz-distribution space. Together with the reduction to irreducible factors and finite-component assembly, these results establish regularity for all symmetric pairs of connected complex reductive groups. We further establish multiplicity one for irreducible Casselman-Wallach representations whenever the complex symmetric space is connected, allowing disconnected ambient groups. In particular, van Dijk's unitary Gelfand conjecture follows in this setting. Finally, we construct an invariant tempered distribution supported on an EVII nilpotent orbit closure whose Fourier transform also has nilpotent support, showing that the EVII isotropy representation is not special.
item.dc:creator: Yuxuan Ge

item.title: Finite Root Sums in Symmetrizable Kac-Moody Algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.15923v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a symmetrizable Kac-Moody algebra with root system $\Phi$. A subset $S\subseteq\Phi$ is \emph{closed} if $\alpha,\beta\in S$ and $\alpha+\beta\in\Phi$ imply $\alpha+\beta\in S$. For finite and affine Kac-Moody algebras, this closure property is known to extend from pairs to arbitrary finite sums that are roots. We prove that every closed subset of the root system of any symmetrizable Kac-Moody algebra is closed under arbitrary finite sums that are roots. The proof uses real-root strings and simultaneous separation of positive imaginary roots, together with an addition lemma for fundamental imaginary roots. As an application, we extend a necessary condition for wideness of regular subalgebras from finite and affine types to all symmetrizable Kac-Moody algebras: the symmetric closure of the roots associated to a wide regular subalgebra is the entire root system.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Douglas

item.title: Singularities of orthogonal and symplectic determinantal varieties
item.description: arXiv:2311.07549v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let either $GL(E)\times SO(F)$ or $GL(E)\times Sp(F)$ act naturally on the space of matrices $E\otimes F$. There are only finitely many orbits, and the orbit closures are orthogonal and symplectic generalizations of determinantal varieties, which can be described similarly using rank conditions. In this paper, we study the singularities of these varieties and describe their defining equations. We prove that in the symplectic case, the orbit closures are normal with good filtrations, and in characteristic $0$ have rational singularities. In the orthogonal case we show that most orbit closures will have similar properties, and determine precisely the exceptions to this.
item.dc:creator: Andr\'as Cristian L\H{o}rincz

item.title: Logarithmic Crystalline Representations
item.description: arXiv:2504.14246v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In 1989, Faltings proved the comparison theorem between \'etale cohomology and crystalline cohomology by studying Fontaine-Faltings modules and crystalline representations. In his paper, he mentioned these modules and representations can be extended to the logarithmic context, but without detail. This note aims to explicitly present the construction of logarithmic Fontaine-Faltings modules and logarithmic crystalline representations.
item.dc:creator: Zhenmou Liu, Jinbang Yang, Kang Zuo

item.title: Cuspidal distinction via intertwining periods
item.description: arXiv:2512.19831v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Local intertwining periods have so far been used to reduce distinction of a general irreducible representation to distinction of cuspidal ones, for which other tools -- type theory, local and global trace formulae -- take over. The main contribution of this paper is to prove that they can be used to decide distinction of cuspidal representations themselves. We develop this approach with three well-studied examples for which the ambient group is an inner form of $\mathrm{GL}_n$ over a $p$-adic field, namely linear models, their non-split twisted version, and the quaternionic symplectic model. As consequences, we obtain proofs valid in arbitrary residual characteristic of the cuspidal case of the epsilon dichotomy conjecture of Prasad and Takloo-Bighash and of Prasad's conjecture on quaternionic symplectic models. The proof in the quaternionic symplectic model case, although going through intertwining periods, uses the simplest ones, namely closed intertwining periods, and is disappointingly short and elementary.
item.dc:creator: Nadir Matringe

item.title: Toric schemes and integral models for Shimura varieties with $\Gamma_1(p)$-type level
item.description: arXiv:2602.23245v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We propose a conjectural theory of $p$-integral models of Shimura varieties with level structure at $p$ given by a class of normal subgroups of parahoric subgroups with abelian quotient group. The role of the theory of local models is played in this context by a certain root stack over the local model for parahoric level. The construction of this root stack is based on the "divisor theorem" (a foundational fact about local models) and on the theory of toric varieties in this context, both of which are of independent interest. We prove our conjecture in the case of Shimura varieties of PEL type when the parahoric is an Iwahori (under some additional conditions).
item.dc:creator: Georgios Pappas, Michael Rapoport

item.title: Equivariant Chow functions and Wonderful Models in type A and B
item.description: arXiv:2610.03138v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove a general inversion formula in the equivariant incidence algebras of geometric lattices that relates the equivariant Chow function with the equivariant super-reduced characteristic function. We apply this result to the case of minimal wonderful models for hyperplane arrangements associated to root systems, with the natural action of the corresponding Weyl group. Applying this formula to type $A$ (i.e. the partition lattices), we recover Getzler's compositional identity in type $A$. In type $B$ (i.e. the signed partition lattice), we recover Henderson's result, expressing the equivariant Chow generating series in terms of the same series in type $A$ and the equivariant characteristic generating series of type $B$. Moreover, we obtain a new compositional identity for the equivariant Chow generating series.
item.dc:creator: Roberto Pagaria, Tommaso Scognamiglio
